newsitem.title: USA: America Online tries to rein in Trojan Horse.
newsitem.headline: America Online tries to rein in Trojan Horse.

text.p: America Online Inc. on Wednesday sought to bolster its defences in a battle with computer hackers with the introduction of "Download Sentry," an automatic warning about the potential danger of some e-mail file attachments.

The system is designed to counter "Trojan Horse" computer programmes, which seek to capture passwords and then e-mail them to hackers, giving the hackers access to private AOL accounts or stored files.

Trojan Horse programmes can also damage subscribers' computer hard drives and might contain "objectionable" files, AOL said in a statement. AOL is the world's biggest online service provider with more than 8 million subscribers.
"The Download Sentry will pop up when a subscriber attempts to download an e-mail with one of the types of file attachments associated with Trojan Horse programmes," AOL said.
Users can also protect themselves by not downloading attachments to e-mail from unknown sources or sources suspected of trying to impersonate known addresses, the company said.
